reference.title: Lying Abduction
reference.listing: Page could not be read here (gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy); the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice.

breathing.pattern: Inhale as the legs open, exhale as you squeeze them back together.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s to open, 2 s to close

prescription.tempo: 2 s open, short pause, 2 s close
prescription.progression: Slower tempo, a longer pause in the open position, then light ankle weights

cues.text: Lie on your back, arms by your sides, and raise both straight legs until they point at the ceiling.
Open the legs out to the sides in a wide V, slowly, keeping them straight and the toes up.
Squeeze the legs back together over the hips.
Keep the low back and the pelvis quiet on the mat for every rep.

mistakes.mistake: Opening so wide that the low back arches or the pelvis rocks
mistakes.fix: Open only as far as the pelvis stays still.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the legs drop apart quickly
mistakes.fix: Control the opening; take 2 s each way.
Keep the knees straight; if the hamstrings are tight, bring the legs a little further from vertical.

mistakes.mistake: Lifting the head and straining the neck
mistakes.fix: Rest the head on the mat.

kinematics.norm: A comfortable wide V, about 30-45 degrees per leg (clinical opinion)
Slow and controlled, about 2 s each way (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #24135, Lying Abduction, video (movement reference; page not readable here)
Andersson, Nilsson, Ma and Thorstensson 1997, abdominal and hip flexor muscle activation during various training exercises (Eur J Appl Physiol 75:115-123; PMID 9118976)
Drysdale, Earl and Hertel 2004, surface EMG of the abdominal muscles during pelvic-tilt and abdominal-hollowing exercises (J Athl Train 39(1):32-36)
Macadam, Cronin & Contreras 2015, gluteal muscle activity in dynamic hip abduction and hip external rotation exercise: a systematic review (Int J Sports Phys Ther 10(5):573-591; PMC4595911)

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
If the low back arches off the mat, the legs are too low for your strength: raise them or bend the knees.
modify: Hands under the buttocks help keep the pelvis tilted and the low back down.
Bend the knees a little to shorten the lever.
Pregnancy, postpartum or diastasis recti: get cleared first, and avoid long supine work later in pregnancy.
regressions: Knees bent, feet on the floor, let the knees fall open and close (butterfly).
progressions: Pause 3 s in the open position.
Side-lying hip abduction for more abductor load.

muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Gluteus medius and the other abductors start each opening and set its pace (clinical opinion; with the legs straight up gravity loads them little, so this is a light abduction drill).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Gluteus medius and the other abductors start each opening and set its pace (clinical opinion; with the legs straight up gravity loads them little, so this is a light abduction drill).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Past vertical, gravity pulls the legs apart: the adductors lengthen to control the opening and shorten to squeeze the legs back together (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Past vertical, gravity pulls the legs apart: the adductors lengthen to control the opening and shorten to squeeze the legs back together (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: Iliopsoas and rectus femoris hold the legs up against gravity (clinical opinion; hip flexor EMG rises with leg-lowering work, Andersson 1997).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_l: Iliopsoas and rectus femoris hold the legs up against gravity (clinical opinion; hip flexor EMG rises with leg-lowering work, Andersson 1997).
muscleNotes.core: Rectus abdominis and transversus abdominis keep the pelvis from tipping forward and the low back from arching while the legs move (Drysdale 2004: highest abdominal activity in pelvic-tilt work with the legs unsupported).
muscleNotes.quads_r: Keep the knees straight and the legs long (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Keep the knees straight and the legs long (clinical opinion).
